clue.text: Lack of ability shown by language associated with Philadelphia?

definitions.meaning: words describing Philadelphia: it lies 'in' a 'PA city', a city of Pennsylvania (PA)

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether the way people talk in Philadelphia betrays some shortcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN + CAPA + CITY, heard as 'in PA city': PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, whose largest city is Philadelphia.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being unable to do something is a want of capability.

clue.text: Slight problem eliminating hot source of irritation

indicators.note: eliminating says the letter for hot is dropped from the word for a slight problem

parts.note: a hitch is a minor snag
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone getting rid of a minor bother by turning down the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin sensation that irritates and makes you want to scratch.

clue.text: Firm, not the first to cut off diplomatic residence

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the cutting-off word is dropped

parts.note: to insulate is to isolate or cut off

explanation.surface: A company, having lost its lead, is told to isolate an embassy building.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the official office and home of a consul, a diplomatic post abroad.

clue.text: Page with note in newspaper showing crash

indicators.note: in puts the note's letter inside the word for a newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid page carrying a note about a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially a minor car or plane accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British informal for a collision or minor accident, a crash.

clue.text: Military figure fit to stop killer

indicators.note: to stop is read as plugging a gap: the fitting word goes in to fill the middle of the killer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A soldier fit enough to halt a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is an army officer rank, so a figure in the military.

clue.text: Time quickly passed before appearance of model route

indicators.note: before places the running word ahead of the model's appearance

parts.note: ran means went quickly
an artist's model sits, attending a sitting

explanation.surface: Time flew before a model turned up for a session about a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit is a passage or way across, hence a route, as in a transit corridor.

clue.text: Young animal's fleshy part

definitions.meaning: a young cow or whale; the 's stands for 'is'
the muscular back of the lower leg

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a young bovine and the meaty back of the human lower leg.

clue.text: Stroll, one bets, avoiding extremities

indicators.note: avoiding extremities says the betting person loses both end letters

parts.note: a gambler is one who bets

explanation.surface: A punter taking a leisurely walk while keeping away from the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at an easy, unhurried pace, a synonym of stroll.

clue.text: One in a race, paddling steel ferry

indicators.note: paddling suggests churning water about, so the letters of steel ferry are stirred up

explanation.surface: A competitor paddling a steel boat in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestyle swimming race has competitors, each a swimmer entered in that event.

clue.text: Waiters mixed up starter of 'escargot' or 'espresso' in manner of speaking

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters of Waiters are jumbled
starter of takes the first letter of the quoted French dish, a pun on a meal's starter

explanation.surface: Confused waiters serving snails or coffee as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or espresso' offers a second word with the same first letter E, so either gives the letter needed after the jumbled Waiters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning so to speak, used when speaking figuratively.

clue.text: Study good area for dance

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Studying a good place for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American line dance in which people follow one another in a chain.

clue.text: Reasonable advantage retaining a religious work originally lost

indicators.note: retaining says the plus holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: a plus is a benefit or advantage

indicators.note: originally lost says the first letter of the holy book is removed

parts.note: the Bible is the Christian holy book

explanation.surface: A sensible benefit kept even though a sacred text was first mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plausible and reasonable both describe a claim that seems believable and fair.

clue.text: Refined head of grenadiers wearing sword

indicators.note: wearing means the sword has the soldier's initial inside it, as though carried on the body

parts.note: a cutlass is a short curved sword

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of grenadiers

explanation.surface: A dignified officer of the Grenadier Guards wearing a ceremonial sword.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut-glass describes a posh, precise upper-class British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to an accent, it means elegant and upper-class, a refined way of speaking.

clue.text: Lock put in fortresses

indicators.note: put in says the word sits inside the letters of fortresses

explanation.surface: A lock fitted in castle strongholds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' wants to be a door lock, given the fortresses; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Block bug with last of some sticky material

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to block it
to tap a phone is to bug it

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of some

explanation.surface: Stopping an insect with the end of something gooey.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch Tape is a brand of adhesive tape, the clear sticky material on a roll.

clue.text: Companion with a smile — or disappointment

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A friend offers either a smile or a let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation from being let down or humiliated.

clue.text: Vehicle accessory surprisingly OK for car

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of OK for car come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An accessory that turns out, unexpectedly, to suit the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame fitted on top of a vehicle to carry luggage, an add-on for a car.

clue.text: What hard nut might take, ending in recovery?

definitions.text: What hard nut might take, ending in recovery?

parts.note: a tough guy might take the rap, accepting blame for a crime

indicators.note: ending in takes the final letter of recovery

explanation.surface: A tough criminal or a crazy person facing the consequences and hoping to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the hard man takes the rap; read whole, a 'nut', a disturbed person, might undergo treatment that ends in recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment for illness, including psychological, meant to bring about recovery.

clue.text: One dissecting a military group on film

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance
a mist is a thin film, as on a window

explanation.surface: Someone analysing an army unit shown in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies body structure, traditionally by cutting up specimens.

clue.text: Fix game in a losing position

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
a side that is down is behind in the score

explanation.surface: Rigging a match when you're behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to secure or fasten something firmly, to fix it in place.

clue.text: North American Latin couple protecting plunder in African city

indicators.note: protecting says the pair of numerals wraps around the plunder

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
to rob is to plunder

explanation.surface: An American and two Latin speakers guarding loot in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, a large East African city.

clue.text: Small space in rank for explosive device

indicators.note: in puts the small space inside the rank

parts.note: a grade is a rank or level
an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em

explanation.surface: A tiny gap in the ranks leaves room for a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, an explosive device.

clue.text: Information on French art is to be used in group

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
es is French for 'art', the old second-person form of 'are'

explanation.surface: Background on French art to be used in a group project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is not painting: in French 'tu es' means 'thou art'. Genesis is the British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known British rock band, so a musical group.

clue.text: Show indecision in Georgian house with number missing

indicators.note: missing says the short form for number goes absent from the royal house

parts.note: the four King Georges belonged to the royal House of Hanover

explanation.surface: Dithering over a Georgian house without a house number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian house' looks like a building; it is the royal dynasty. Haver is chiefly British and Scottish for dither.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to dither or waver, unable to decide.

clue.text: Runabout needed after very excessive consumption of drugs and drink

indicators.note: after places the small car at the end, following the other two pieces

parts.note: OD is short for overdose
the Ka is a small Ford car, a runabout

explanation.surface: A car is required after someone overdoes the drugs and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Key is required for this part of estate, say

definitions.text: Key is required for this part of estate, say

parts.words: Key is required for this part of estate, say
parts.note: an estate is a British name for a station wagon, and in such a car you turn a key in this part to start the engine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests land; it is an estate car, British for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The switch that starts a car's engine, operated with a key.

clue.text: Voluntary lot audibly disapprove of ritual restriction

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to boo is to show disapproval vocally

explanation.surface: Volunteers loudly objecting to a ceremonial ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a ban rooted in custom or ritual.

clue.text: Present picked up for judge

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the word for present is taken by its sound

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A judge collecting a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case, so to hear is to try it.

clue.text: Daring account produced in car by old American

indicators.note: produced in places the account's letters inside the car

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

explanation.surface: A bold report written in an old American's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious means bold and willing to take risks.

clue.text: Bit of butter in cheese making grease

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: Bit of takes the first letter of butter

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene of butter mixed into cheese to make a fatty mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grease' reads as a noun; it is the verb in 'grease someone's palm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease a palm is an idiom for paying someone off.

clue.text: Dash from tailless animal

indicators.note: tailless says the antelope loses its last letter

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A tailless creature dashing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan and dash both mean flair and spirited style.

clue.text: Prisoner misbehaving around extremists in riot, a furious affair

indicators.note: around says the shuffled prisoner goes about the riot's end letters
misbehaving says the letters of Prisoner are thrown out of order
extremists in takes the outside letters of riot

explanation.surface: An unruly inmate surrounded by agitators in a riot, a wild event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts RIPSNOER (the anagram of Prisoner, from 'misbehaving') round RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-snorter is something wild and vigorous, a rowdy or violent occasion.
